title: What should the two friends do to find the most popular game?
description: Two friends want to know the most popular game in their class. The video shows how to gather every child's answer into a list, and Keeko doubts whether one friend's favourite can stand for the whole class.
teaching_notes: One idea: to learn what a group prefers, ask each member and record the answers. Watch for children who answer from their own liking instead of asking everyone.

source: To figure out the most popular game in their class, what should the two friends do?
video_script.why: The child sees that asking every member and writing the answers down is how data is collected.
video_script.substitution: none: the book's own question about the favourite-games list
video_script.anchor: Ziva and Laksh planning the favourite-games list for their class
video_script.wrong_answer: the favourite of one friend is the favourite of the class
video_script.wrong_move: takes one friend's liking as the answer for the whole class
video_script.payoff_line: They should ask every classmate for a favourite game and write the answers in a list.

final_answer.value: Ask each classmate for the favourite game and record the answers in a list
final_answer.spoken: ask every classmate and write the answers in a list

names.Ziva: girl who makes the favourite-games list with Naresh
names.Laksh: boy who collects favourite games with Navya

maths_rules: The class list has one favourite game for each child.
No count is made in this video; counting comes in the next one.
video_script.design: The two friends, a class of children, and a list that fills with one line for each child.

beats.on_screen: title card with the two friends facing a row of classmates, each with a blank speech bubble

marks.friends: the two friends step in front of the row of classmates
marks.ask: a question mark lights up above the row

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about Ziva and Laksh.
<bookmark mark='friends'/>Ziva likes cricket, but Laksh likes hockey the most.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>They want to find the most popular game in their class.
What should they do?

beats.on_screen: the row of classmates and the question mark stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a card reads: a collection of facts about things is data; a few facts about games are shown as small pictures

marks.facts: the small pictures of games appear as facts
marks.name: the word data is written on the card

narration: <bookmark mark='facts'/>The favourite game of each child is a fact about that child.
<bookmark mark='name'/>Any collection of facts that tells us about things is called data.
Getting these facts from many children means collecting data.

beats.on_screen: Given: two friends, one class, many favourite games
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the two friends and one class with many favourite games.

beats.on_screen: To find: what the friends should do

marks.find: the line to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find what the friends should do to see the most popular game.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: go to each child in the class and ask for a favourite game

marks.go: an arrow runs from the friends to each child in turn
marks.own: every child gets a small bubble of their own

narration: <bookmark mark='go'/>Step one, go to each child in the class and ask for a favourite game.
<bookmark mark='own'/>Every child has a favourite of their own, so every child must be asked.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: write each child's name and game on one line of a list

marks.write: one line of the list is written for each child

narration: <bookmark mark='write'/>Step two, write each answer in a list, one line for each child.
Then no answer is lost or forgotten.

beats.on_screen: Answer: ask every classmate and write the answers in a list; this is collecting data
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>They should ask every classmate for a favourite game and write the answers in a list.
This is how the friends collect their data.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a cricket bubble above one friend with a tick, crossed out, and many other bubbles of different games around it

marks.doubt: the cricket bubble appears with a tick
marks.fix: the other bubbles of different games appear around it

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the favourite of one friend is the favourite of the class.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But Laksh likes hockey, and other children may like other games.
One child cannot speak for everyone, so we must ask the whole class.
